newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX to launch advertising blitz.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX to launch advertising blitz.

text.p: NYNEX Corp will launch a sales blitz in early 1997 for value-added services like Caller ID, voice-dialing and call-waiting, Chief Executive Ivan Seidenberg said Tuesday.
"To jump-start 1997 we will in a couple of days announce a sales blitz," Seidenberg told a Salomon Bros investor conference.
"Our goal is to sell an additional one million features," he said.
Seidenberg said NYNEX's aim was to increase revenues by boosting the average value of customers to the company, even while some customers are lost because of increased competition.
"We will lose some market share but we will increase revenues," he said
He said that as more features and functions -- from video to the Internet -- became available, opportunity grows to boost average revenue per customer.
He said NYNEX had increased the number of second lines by 12 percent so far in 1996, while the number of Caller ID features in service had risen 30 percent.
He said that despite the effect of competition in IntraLATA (medium-distance) calling, which began in the first quarter of 1996, NYNEX has continued to increase revenues in that market place.
He said NYNEX had sold $1.7 million IntraLATA calling plans in six months, and revenues had risen four percent in that sector despite the loss of some customers.
On top of this, NYNEX has recaptured some revenues from rivals through a 30 percent increase in its wholesale business sector, he said.
Seidenberg said businesses were now outsourcing some of the telecommunication functions to NYNEX that had previously been taken in-house. This has boosted sales of Centrex circuits, he said.
"Centrex is doing absolutely great," Seidenberg said.
